cards.title: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS)
cards.body: Program 4 · Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing I

cards.title: Welcome to Program 4
cards.body: Adult medical-surgical nursing sits at the heart of everyday hospital practice. Nurses care for adults experiencing acute illness, long-term conditions, surgery, pain, reduced mobility and changing physical function.

bullets.label: This programme develops the practical
bullets.text: This programme develops the practical knowledge, clinical reasoning and professional behaviours required to assess adults, plan care, recognise deterioration and deliver safe interventions across hospital, clinic and community settings.

bullets.label: Complete a structured head-to-toe adult patient assessment
Relate common symptoms to underlying body system changes
Prepare patients for surgery and deliver safe postoperative care

cards.title: Why This Learning Matters
cards.body: Adult patients rarely present with a single problem. A person admitted with pneumonia may also have diabetes, reduced mobility and kidney impairment — all at the same time.

bullets.label: Nurses must connect assessment findings,
bullets.text: Nurses must connect assessment findings, identify the most urgent need and coordinate care — without losing sight of the patient's comfort, dignity and goals.

bullets.label: Holistic nursing means treating the whole person, not just the diagnosis.

cards.title: SECTION 1
cards.body: Foundations of Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing

bullets.label: Nursing addresses how disease affects the person — physically, emotionally, socially and functionally.
Understanding how illness alters body function helps nurses interpret symptoms and anticipate complications.
Assess → Identify → Plan → Implement → Evaluate. Continuous, not a one-time written exercise.
Airway, breathing and circulation guide urgent decisions. Safety and life-threatening concerns come first.

cards.title: The Nursing Process
cards.body: Assessment

bullets.label: The nursing process is a continuous clinical
bullets.text: The nursing process is a continuous clinical cycle — not a one-time exercise. Each stage informs the next, ensuring care remains safe, responsive and person-centred throughout the patient's journey.

cards.title: Clinical Example — Mr Singh
cards.body: Admitted with pneumonia: fever, productive cough, low oxygen saturation and weakness. The nurse first addresses breathing — positions him upright, applies prescribed oxygen and completes respiratory assessment. Hydration, medication, mobility and education follow, all prioritised by immediate risk while remaining person-centred.

bullets.label: Treat the person, not only the diagnosis
Use pathophysiology to interpret assessment findings
Prioritise airway, breathing, circulation and immediate safety

cards.title: SECTION 2
cards.body: Comprehensive Assessment & Clinical Reasoning

bullets.label: A thorough assessment provides the foundation
bullets.text: A thorough assessment provides the foundation for every nursing decision. Adult patients may deteriorate gradually — early clues can be subtle.

bullets.label: Presenting problem, medications, allergies, cognition, nutrition and social circumstances
Systematic head-to-toe: airway, breathing, circulation, skin, abdomen, mobility
A single reading may appear normal — a trend may reveal deterioration

cards.title: Recognising Deterioration — Early Warning Signs
cards.body: Rising Respiratory Rate

bullets.label: An increasing respiratory rate is often the
bullets.text: An increasing respiratory rate is often the earliest sign of clinical deterioration — observe trends, not single readings.

bullets.label: Unexplained increase in heart rate may signal pain, bleeding, infection or cardiovascular compromise.
Falling urine output may indicate dehydration, reduced kidney perfusion or developing shock.
New or worsening confusion is a red flag — assess oxygenation, blood glucose, infection and medication effects.
Escalate concerns before severe deterioration occurs — act on trends, not just single abnormal values.

cards.title: Clinical Example — Mrs Chen
cards.body: Recovering from abdominal surgery. Blood pressure remains within normal range — but respiratory rate has risen, urine output has fallen and she appears restless. The nurse recognises the trend, repeats observations, assesses the wound and fluid balance, and escalates promptly.

bullets.label: Key lesson: A normal blood pressure alone does not mean a patient is safe. Always assess the full clinical picture.

cards.title: SECTION 3
cards.body: Nursing Care for Common Medical Conditions

bullets.label: Monitor pain, fluid balance, activity tolerance
bullets.text: Monitor pain, fluid balance, activity tolerance and medication response. Escalate chest pain, hypotension or arrhythmia urgently.

bullets.label: Asthma, COPD, pneumonia. Positioning, oxygen therapy, inhaled treatments, hydration and sputum management.
Accurate intake/output, daily weight, blood pressure and oedema assessment for kidney impairment.
Blood glucose monitoring, medication safety, nutrition, foot care and recognition of hypo- or hyperglycaemia.

cards.title: Clinical Example — Mr Ali
cards.body: Mr Ali has heart failure and diabetes. He becomes more breathless, gains 2 kg in three days and develops ankle swelling.

bullets.label: Fluid balance, oxygen saturation, lung sounds and blood glucose
Administer prescribed therapy and escalate the clinical change
Teach the patient why daily weight monitoring is critical for self-management

cards.title: SECTION 4
cards.body: Surgical Nursing & Prevention of Complications

bullets.label: Surgical nursing begins before the procedure
bullets.text: Surgical nursing begins before the procedure and continues through recovery and discharge. Nurses prepare patients physically and emotionally, confirm safety requirements and prevent complications at every stage.

cards.title: Preventing Postoperative Complications
cards.body: Deep Breathing & Coughing

bullets.label: Reduces risk of atelectasis and chest infection
Prevents venous thromboembolism, pressure injuries and muscle weakness
Prevents surgical site infection with sterile technique and regular assessment
Effective pain relief enables breathing, movement and rest — essential for recovery
Clinical Example: Ms Brown reports calf pain
bullets.text: Clinical Example: Ms Brown reports calf pain and swelling post knee surgery. The nurse recognises possible VTE, stops mobilisation, escalates urgently and follows the clinical pathway. Early recognition prevents treatment delay.

cards.title: Your Learning Goal — Level 1 Complete
cards.body: By completing GNPS Program 4 — Level 1, you have developed the foundational knowledge and clinical skills to:

bullets.label: Assess adults with common medical and surgical conditions
Develop safe, individualised nursing care plans
Recognise and respond to early signs of deterioration
NEXT: LEVEL 2 — INTERNATIONAL QUALIFIED NURSE · COMPLEX CARE · MULTIDISCIPLINARY COORDINATION

cards.title: Section 1: Foundations of Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing
cards.body: Introduction

bullets.label: Adult medical-surgical nursing focuses on
bullets.text: Adult medical-surgical nursing focuses on caring for people who experience acute illness, chronic disease, injury, or surgery. Effective care addresses not only the clinical condition, but also pain, mobility, nutrition, emotional wellbeing, family support, and discharge readiness.

bullets.label: All care is organised through the nursing
bullets.text: All care is organised through the nursing process: assessment, problem identification, planning, implementation, and evaluation.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: After completing this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Explain the scope of adult medical-surgical nursing
Describe each stage of the nursing process
Relate pathophysiology to common clinical manifestations
Identify factors that influence an adult patient's response to illness

cards.title: The Adult Patient as a Whole Person
cards.body: A medical diagnosis describes the disease — nursing care addresses how that disease affects the person. Assessment must consider physical, psychological, social, cultural, and functional dimensions.

bullets.label: May reduce mobility and disrupt sleep
May limit coughing or movement after surgery
Financial or family concerns can hinder recovery

cards.title: Pathophysiology & Clinical Presentation
cards.body: Understanding how a condition alters normal body function helps the nurse interpret symptoms and anticipate complications before they escalate.

bullets.label: When nurses understand the underlying mechanism, they can:
Educate patients on what to expect
Collaborate effectively with the medical team
Pathophysiology knowledge bridges the gap
bullets.text: Pathophysiology knowledge bridges the gap between knowing a diagnosis and understanding its impact on the individual patient.

cards.title: The Nursing Process
cards.body: Assessment

bullets.label: The nursing process is continuous — not a
bullets.text: The nursing process is continuous — not a single written exercise. Each stage informs the next, and evaluation loops back to reassessment, ensuring care remains responsive and evidence-based throughout the patient's journey.

cards.title: Prioritisation in Clinical Practice
cards.body: Frameworks for Safe Decision-Making

bullets.label: The immediate framework for any urgent or deteriorating patient
New or worsening findings take precedence over stable, long-standing issues
Unstable patients require continuous monitoring and rapid escalation
Unexpected changes signal potential complications requiring immediate action

cards.title: Clinical Example: Mr Singh
cards.body: DIAGNOSIS: PNEUMONIA

bullets.label: Fever, productive cough, low oxygen saturation, and weakness on admission
Position upright, apply prescribed oxygen, and complete respiratory assessment
Hydration, prescribed medication, graded mobility, and patient education
Clinical priorities are balanced with Mr Singh's individual needs and preferences

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Treat the Whole Person

bullets.label: Address not only the diagnosis, but the person's physical, emotional, and social experience of illness
Use your understanding of disease mechanisms to interpret findings and anticipate problems
Apply assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation continuously — not just at admission
Airway, breathing, and circulation guide every urgent clinical decision

cards.title: Ready to Progress?
cards.body: You have completed Section 1: Foundations of Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing. These core principles underpin every clinical scenario you will encounter in Sections 2–5 and in your NCLEX preparation.

bullets.label: Revisit the nursing process stages and prioritisation framework
Consider how pathophysiology shaped Mr Singh's nursing priorities
Proceed to Section 2: Caring for Patients with Respiratory Conditions

cards.title: Comprehensive Assessment & Clinical Reasoning
cards.body: GNPS Program 4 · Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing I

bullets.label: Section 2 — Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) · Level 3

cards.title: Why This Section Matters
cards.body: Assessment Is the Foundation of Every Nursing Decision

bullets.label: Adult patients can deteriorate gradually, and
bullets.text: Adult patients can deteriorate gradually, and early warning signs are often subtle. A structured, thorough assessment gives nurses the information they need to act before a situation becomes critical.

bullets.label: Clinical reasoning means more than collecting
bullets.text: Clinical reasoning means more than collecting data — it means interpreting what the data means and deciding what to do next, in the right order.

bullets.label: Early recognition saves lives. Assessment is not a one-time task — it is a continuous process.

cards.title: Learning Outcomes
cards.body: By the end of this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Conduct a systematic head-to-toe physical assessment
Distinguish normal from abnormal clinical findings confidently
Analyse trends in vital signs and basic investigations
Use clinical reasoning to identify and act on priority nursing problems

cards.title: Core Concept 1
cards.body: History & Baseline

bullets.label: Knowing the patient's usual condition is
bullets.text: Knowing the patient's usual condition is essential — it makes new changes far easier to recognise. A thorough history should cover:

cards.title: Core Concept 2
cards.body: Head-to-Toe Physical Assessment

bullets.label: A systematic approach ensures no system is
bullets.text: A systematic approach ensures no system is overlooked. Findings must be recorded objectively and compared with previous observations.

bullets.label: Respiratory rate, effort, oxygen saturation, breath sounds
Heart rate, blood pressure, skin colour, capillary refill, peripheral pulses
Level of consciousness, orientation, confusion, GCS if indicated
Wound condition, bowel sounds, pressure areas, assistive devices

cards.title: Core Concept 3
cards.body: Vital Signs & Trends — Look Beyond the Single Reading

bullets.label: A single observation may appear acceptable in
bullets.text: A single observation may appear acceptable in isolation, while a trend reveals deterioration. Train yourself to look for combinations and direction of change over time.

bullets.label: Could indicate pain, sepsis, or hypovolaemia
Sensitive indicator of fluid status and renal perfusion
May signal hypoxia, infection, or haemodynamic compromise

cards.title: Core Concept 4
cards.body: Interpreting Diagnostic Information

bullets.label: Laboratory and diagnostic results support —
bullets.text: Laboratory and diagnostic results support — they do not replace — clinical assessment. Understand the clinical meaning of these common investigations within your scope of practice.

cards.title: Clinical Example — Mrs Chen
cards.body: Mrs Chen is recovering from abdominal surgery. Her blood pressure remains within normal range — but her respiratory rate has risen, urine output has fallen, and she appears restless.

bullets.label: Check wound, fluid balance, repeat obs
The nurse does not wait for the blood pressure
bullets.text: The nurse does not wait for the blood pressure to fall. The trend — not a single value — triggers timely assessment and escalation. This is clinical reasoning in action.

cards.title: The Clinical Reasoning Process
cards.body: From Cues to Action

bullets.label: Gather history, observations, and diagnostic data systematically
What has changed from the patient's normal or previous readings?
What could explain this combination of findings?
Intervene at your scope level and escalate concerns promptly

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Know the Baseline

bullets.label: Establish the patient's usual condition — changes are only meaningful against a known normal
A structured head-to-toe approach prevents missed findings — never rely on a single symptom
Look for direction of change over time and patterns across multiple parameters
Act before severe deterioration occurs — early escalation improves patient outcomes
NCLEX Tip: Questions often test your ability to
bullets.text: NCLEX Tip: Questions often test your ability to recognise early deterioration and select the priority nursing action — escalation and reassessment are frequently correct responses.

decks.title: Nursing Care for Common Medical Conditions
decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 4 - Level 1 - Section 3 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing I
cards.body: Global Nursing Professional Series (GNPS) — Program 4

bullets.label: Section 3: Nursing Care for Common Medical Conditions

cards.title: What You Will Learn
cards.body: By the end of this section, you will be able to confidently care for adults with common medical conditions across five key body systems.

bullets.label: Identify nursing priorities for common adult medical conditions
Track treatment response and recognise early complications
Deliver safe fluid, oxygen, nutrition and medication care
Support self-management and health promotion strategies

cards.title: Cardiovascular Conditions
cards.body: Hypertension, coronary artery disease and heart failure are among the most common conditions nurses manage in adult wards.

bullets.label: Pain, circulation, fluid balance and activity tolerance
Response to medications, blood pressure and heart rhythm
New chest pain, severe breathlessness, hypotension or arrhythmia

cards.title: Respiratory Conditions
cards.body: Asthma · COPD · Pneumonia

bullets.label: These conditions reduce oxygenation and increase the work of breathing. Timely, structured nursing care is critical.
Oxygen therapy: As prescribed; monitor saturation
Sputum management: Encourage hydration and expectoration
Watch for: Fatigue, worsening effort or respiratory failure

cards.title: Renal & Fluid Balance
cards.body: Acute or chronic kidney impairment disrupts fluid regulation, electrolyte levels and medication clearance — requiring precise, consistent monitoring.

bullets.label: Detect fluid gain or loss early

cards.title: Gastrointestinal & Endocrine Conditions
cards.body: GI Assessment

bullets.label: Assess for abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding
bullets.text: Assess for abdominal pain, vomiting, bleeding and altered bowel function. Monitor nutritional intake and escalate signs of deterioration.

bullets.label: Regular blood glucose checks, safe insulin or
bullets.text: Regular blood glucose checks, safe insulin or medication administration, and early recognition of hypo- or hyperglycaemia.

bullets.label: Inspect feet for wounds, pressure or infection. Diabetes impairs healing — prevention and early detection are essential.

cards.title: Clinical Example: Mr Ali
cards.body: "He becomes more breathless, gains 2 kg in three days and develops ankle swelling."

bullets.label: This case illustrates how two conditions interact, and why holistic assessment matters.
Intake, output and daily weight trend
O₂ saturation, lung sounds, blood glucose
Explain the importance of daily weight monitoring

cards.title: Nursing Assessment Across Systems
cards.body: Each body system requires a targeted yet connected approach. Use this framework to structure your clinical thinking.

bullets.label: Evaluate symptoms and vital signs promptly.
Track trends and review lab results.
Provide care and escalate as needed.
This cycle repeats with every patient contact — linking observation to action to outcomes.

cards.title: Red Flag Recognition
cards.body: Timely escalation saves lives. Know when to act — these signs require urgent review regardless of the body system involved.

bullets.label: New chest pain, hypotension, arrhythmia, severe breathlessness
Increasing effort, falling O₂ saturation, exhaustion, silent chest
Sudden fluid overload, oliguria, rising creatinine or potassium
Severe hypoglycaemia, DKA signs, uncontrolled hyperglycaemia

cards.title: Key Learning Points
cards.body: Carry these principles into every shift — they underpin safe, effective medical-surgical nursing.

bullets.label: Link what you observe to the underlying condition and pathophysiology
Track both progression of illness and the patient's response to interventions
These are vital, objective clinical indicators — chart them accurately every shift
Empowered patients detect deterioration earlier and manage conditions better
NCLEX Tip: Prioritisation questions often test
bullets.text: NCLEX Tip: Prioritisation questions often test whether you can identify the most urgent finding and the most appropriate nursing action — practise applying these principles to clinical scenarios.

decks.sourceFile: GNPS Program 4 - Level 1 - Section 4 Qualified Nurse - Presentation deck.pptx

cards.title: Surgical Nursing and Prevention of Complications
cards.body: GNPS Programme 4 · Adult Medical-Surgical Nursing I · Level 1 — Qualified Nurse

cards.title: Global Nursing Professional Series
cards.body: What You Will Learn in This Section

bullets.label: Surgical nursing spans every phase — from
bullets.text: Surgical nursing spans every phase — from pre-operative preparation to safe discharge. By the end of this section, you will be able to:

bullets.label: Ready an adult patient for surgery with confidence
Support recovery through pain relief, breathing and mobility

cards.title: Preoperative Care: Setting the Foundation for Safety
cards.body: Surgical safety begins well before the patient enters the theatre. Preoperative nursing is a systematic process covering all critical safety checkpoints.

bullets.label: Confirm patient identity, valid signed consent and procedure details
Check fasting status, allergies, medications and investigations
Reduce anxiety through clear communication and patient education

cards.title: Immediate Postoperative Assessment
cards.body: On return from theatre, a structured ABCDE assessment is your first priority. Every finding must be compared with the patient's preoperative baseline and the procedure performed.

bullets.label: A blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg may be normal
bullets.text: A blood pressure of 100/60 mmHg may be normal for one patient and a red flag for another. Always interpret findings in context — the procedure type, anaesthetic used, and the patient's premorbid status all influence expected recovery parameters.

bullets.label: Escalate early. Subtle changes in consciousness
bullets.text: Escalate early. Subtle changes in consciousness or urine output can signal serious complications before overt signs appear.

cards.title: Core Complication Prevention
cards.body: Preventing Postoperative Complications

bullets.label: Deep breathing, coughing exercises and incentive spirometry reduce atelectasis and pneumonia risk
Getting patients up and moving — even briefly — significantly reduces VTE risk and aids recovery
Aseptic wound technique and regular repositioning prevent infection and pressure injuries
Adequate fluids, compression stockings and anticoagulants form a multi-layered thrombosis prevention strategy

cards.title: The Role of Pain Management in Recovery
cards.body: Pain is More Than Discomfort

bullets.label: Undertreated pain prevents patients from
bullets.text: Undertreated pain prevents patients from breathing deeply, mobilising safely, and resting adequately — directly increasing the risk of respiratory, thromboembolic and wound complications.

bullets.label: Assess pain regularly using a validated tool (e.g. NRS 0–10)
Use a multimodal approach: analgesia, positioning, distraction

cards.title: Clinical Example: Recognising VTE
cards.body: After knee surgery, Ms Brown reports increasing calf pain and swelling. This is a classic presentation requiring immediate action.

bullets.label: Identify unilateral calf pain, swelling and warmth as possible DVT
Stop unnecessary mobilisation; perform full limb assessment
Urgently notify the medical team and follow the clinical pathway
Record findings, escalation time and interventions accurately
Early recognition of VTE prevents progression
bullets.text: Early recognition of VTE prevents progression to potentially fatal pulmonary embolism. Never delay escalation when symptoms are present.

cards.title: Recovery and Safe Discharge
cards.body: Discharge planning begins on admission. Effective discharge reduces readmissions and empowers patients to manage their recovery safely at home.

bullets.label: How to clean and dress the wound; signs of infection to watch for
Dosage, timing, side effects and what to do if a dose is missed
Graded return to activity, dietary guidance and hydration targets
Scheduled reviews and red flags that require urgent medical attention

cards.title: NCLEX Focus
cards.body: Key Points for Examination Success

bullets.label: What the NCLEX Expects You to Know
Surgical safety starts before the operation — preoperative checks are a nurse-led responsibility
Always prioritise Airway, Breathing, Circulation in the immediate postoperative period
Evidence-based early actions — breathing exercises, mobilisation, VTE prophylaxis — prevent complications
Clear discharge teaching on warning signs is a core nursing obligation before every patient goes home

cards.title: Section 4 Complete
cards.body: You have covered the full surgical nursing journey — from preoperative preparation and immediate recovery assessment, through complication prevention, to safe and informed discharge.

bullets.label: GNPS Programme 4 · Section 5: Caring for Adults with Chronic Conditions
Review NCLEX-style questions on surgical complications and postoperative priorities
Consider a surgical patient you have cared for — how does this framework apply?
